newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No panic, just healthy dip for Bel-20 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: No panic, just healthy dip for Bel-20 -dealers.

text.p: The Bel-20 index of leading shares slipped more than one percent in cautious early trade on Monday but dealers said it was just the extension of a healthy dip.
At 0840 GMT, the Bel-20 was down 0.77 percent, or 2,516.53 points after earlier dropping to 2,508.79. The index had already lost 1.68 percent on Friday.

"People have woken up again to the fact that shares can actually drop so everybody's a bit nervous and uncertain. But such a dip is healthy, even necessary," one trader said. He added the Bel-20 was unlikely to drop below 2,500 points.
"We've probably seen the worst now," one trader said.

He said the upward trend for the Bel-20 remained intact but that the index was about the embark on the last leg of the bull run. "We're in the speculative stage but there will be no major correction for now...perhaps in October," he said.
Chemicals firm Solvay was down 1.3 percent at 22,700 francs, hurt partly by continuing disappointment at news last week of a first-half profit rise of just three percent.
Oil and gas group PetroFina was dragged 0.5 percent lower to 15,325 despite a 61-percent rise in first-half profits announced last week.

Chemicals and drugs firm UCB, which already shed nearly 12 percent last week when first-half results in line with expectations still disappointed the market, was down 1.4 percent at 128,200 francs after earlier touching 127,950.
